subject: Software Quality

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: ResetTestingAsync mixes multiple responsibilities in one method (maintainability)

evidence.excerpt: public async Task<RetrieveResponse<int>> ResetTestingAsync(...) { ... try { ... connection.Open(); ... transaction.BeginTransaction(); ... try { ... transaction.Commit()/Rollback(); } catch (Exception exInner) { ... } finally { connection.Close(); } ... } catch (UserException) { throw; } catch (Exception ex) { ... } }

findings.recommendation: Extract connection/transaction lifecycle management (open, begin/commit/rollback, close) into a small private helper or a using-based unit-of-work so ResetTestingAsync only orchestrates the high-level steps; this also lets the resource-management code be reused/tested independently.

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: Nested try/catch/finally with multiple branch points increases cyclomatic complexity

evidence.excerpt: try { ... if (activeDataSource == null) ... if (connection.State != ConnectionState.Open) ... try { ... if (result == 0) { transaction.Commit(); } else { transaction.Rollback(); } } catch (Exception exInner) { ... } finally { connection.Close(); } } catch (UserException) { throw; } catch (Exception ex) { ... }

findings.recommendation: Flatten the nested try/catch (e.g. by wrapping connection/transaction/command in `using`/`await using` declarations) and let a single outer catch translate any exception to UserException; this reduces the number of independent paths a reader must trace and removes the manual connection.Close() in a finally block.

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: Data-source-type switch/case structure is duplicated across three private methods

evidence.excerpt: return dataSourceType.ToLowerInvariant() switch { "sqlserver" => new SqlConnection(connectionString), "postgresql" => new NpgsqlConnection(connectionString), _ => throw new ConfigurationException(...) };

return dataSourceType.ToLowerInvariant() switch { "sqlserver" => SqlConstants.SqlServerResetTestingScript, "postgresql" => SqlConstants.PostgreSqlResetTestingScript, _ => throw new ConfigurationException(...) };

findings.recommendation: Consolidate the repeated "sqlserver"/"postgresql" switch into a single per-provider abstraction (e.g. a small IDataSourceProvider implemented once per database type, exposing connection-string building, connection creation and the reset script) so adding a third database only touches one place instead of three near-identical switch statements.

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: Namespace/folder naming is inconsistent for the Domain response model
findings.recommendation: Rename the namespace to PilotUtilityApi.Domain.Models.Responses to match the physical folder (Models/Responses), or move the file into a Dto folder; also note every src project folder is named PilotUtiltyApi.* (missing an 'i') while the namespaces are correctly PilotUtilityApi.* — align folder names with the namespace spelling to avoid confusion.

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: Temporary service provider built before the container is finalized (DI anti-pattern)
findings.standard: Fallback rubric (no single wording-based source for DP-* checks)
findings.recommendation: Avoid calling builder.Services.BuildServiceProvider() before WebApplicationBuilder.Build(): it creates an extra, throwaway DI container whose singletons (e.g. IApplicationConfiguration or anything registered before this point) are separate instances from the ones the running app will later resolve — the same anti-pattern flagged by the ASP0000 analyzer. Read IApplicationConfiguration directly from builder.Configuration/the already-bound settings object, or defer OpenTelemetry/OpenApi configuration to IPostConfigureOptions/IConfigureOptions so no extra container is built.

findings.subject: Software Quality
findings.title: No retry/resilience pattern around external database calls
findings.standard: Azure Architecture Center — Cloud Design Patterns
findings.recommendation: Wrap the connection open/transaction/command sequence with a transient-fault retry policy (e.g. Polly, or the SqlClient/Npgsql built-in retry executors) so brief network blips against SQL Server/PostgreSQL don't surface as user-facing 500s. This may overlap with review-reliability's findings for the same file; aggregation will de-duplicate.
